chapter: England, Paris and memories of Kansas City and Harlem
title: A week at Connie's Inn after Waller
summary: At Connie's Inn her swinging feet fascinated the dancers; she earned $75 a week, which helped the stranded group.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: O.K., do you want to stop a minute? Now then, that time when Fats Waller threw you up in the air, what happened then?

I got a job in - it wasn't the Cotton Club, it was Connie's Inn and they had me there for one week and the people didn't dance or eat because I was so short, my feet was about 6 inches from the floor and everybody was

looking at my feet. I'd get on the tip end of the piano stool. My foot would start bouncing up so high, they'd watch that. Nobody ate and they'd dance right in front of the piano and stop. So I got a job, paying good money too. Well, $75 a week was like $1200 then.
(NOT CLEAR) But it was just a week?

Yes, and it also helped. We were practically stranded and we were out of work. It was during the period after Seymour died and we didn't have any work coming in. Nobody was working so that helped me to give the boys some money. So when I played and worked I gave them some of the money.
